_about: The words of the page's tips (WebUI.js showTip).  page: a button's tip, named by its data-tip-id; {name} is filled from its data-tip-args.  settings: one per parameter, by key; the title, unit, key, the file's value and the wiki link are added from the parameter itself.  A tip has t (one plain line), and may have o (choices: [value, what it does]; the file's value is marked), f (facts: [label, value]), n (a note), kbd (keys), img (a picture of 'pictures', in tooltips/, copied by build_site.py from docs/tooltipsPictures).  A parameter missing here shows its parameter file's comment instead.

Board.t: The laminate: its thickness, dielectrics, outline and holes.

SolderMask.t: The solder mask on both faces: its thickness, openings and edges.

Silkscreen.t: The legend ink, and how its text is drawn.

Finish.t: The surface finish on the copper the mask leaves bare.

Geometry.t: Numerical quality: how finely curves are drawn and how layers share exact edges.
Geometry.n: None of these change any size.

Color.t: The colour of every part in GLB and OBJ files, and of the parts in STEP.

Parallel.t: How many processor cores work at once, and how much the work holds in memory.
Parallel.n: None of these change the model.

Step.t: The STEP files: true arcs and cylinders, and what counts as an arc.

Verifier.t: Checks the finished model: closed solids, matching volumes, no overlaps.

presets.elmer: STEP solids in mm, one per net, without the finish, for gmsh and Elmer.

presets.openems: One STL per part in mm, one per net, without the finish, for openEMS.

o: Every layer a closed solid at its true height, for EM solvers and CAD.
Only the surface you can see, for web viewers and Blender.

Run.UNITS.t: The length unit inside the written files.
o: For STEP, CAD tools and EM solvers.
For GLB viewers, which expect metres.

Run.ORIGIN.t: Where (0, 0) is in the written files.
o: The middle of the board's outline.
KiCad's own origin, so coordinates match the layout and the Gerbers.

Run.ORIENTATION.t: How the board lies in the written files.
o: In XY, F.Cu facing +Z, as in KiCad's top view.
In XZ, F.Cu facing +Y, as the Blender presets use.

Run.WRITE_MATERIALS_JSON.t: Also write materials.json: each part's material, thickness, εr, tan δ, conductivity, net and layer.

Run.EXPORT_INCLUDE_NORMALS.t: Write vertex normals into the GLB. OBJ files always have them.

Run.EXPORT_SET_BUFFERVIEW_TARGETS.t: Mark each GLB buffer with its use, which keeps the Khronos glTF validator free of hints.

Run.SMOOTH_SHADE_ANGLE_DEG.t: Edges sharper than this stay crisp; flatter ones, such as cylinder walls, shade smooth.

Run.TESTED_COPPER_LAYERS.t: A board with more copper layers than this gets a warning. It is still modelled.
Run.TESTED_COPPER_LAYERS.n: 8 is the most among the boards KESE is tested with.

Board.DIELECTRIC_GROUPING.t: How the laminate is split into parts, in Simulation mode.
o: One part per core and prepreg, each with its own material.
The whole laminate as one part.

Board.BOARD_ENABLED.t: Build the laminate and write it to every file.

o: Taken from the board, so the finished board matches KiCad's thickness.
Board.BOARD_THICKNESS_MM.n: With None: the stack-up's dielectrics, or else KiCad's board thickness less the outer copper and the masks.

Board.DEFAULT_BOARD_THICKNESS_MM.t: The finished board's thickness when the file gives none.

Board.DIELECTRIC_SPLIT.t: How the laminate is shared between copper layers when the board has no stack-up.
o: The same thickness between every pair of copper layers.

Board.DEFAULT_DIELECTRIC_TYPE.t: Whether such a dielectric counts as a core or a prepreg.

Board.USE_STACKUP_EPSILON_R.t: Use the stack-up's εr where it has one.
o: Default Epsilon R only fills the gaps.

Board.USE_STACKUP_LOSS_TANGENT.t: Use the stack-up's tan δ where it has one.
o: Default Loss Tangent only fills the gaps.

Board.RESIN_FILL_BETWEEN_INNER_COPPER.t: Resin from the neighbouring prepreg fills the space beside inner copper, as in a pressed board.

Board.INCLUDE_NON_PLATED_HOLES.t: Cut non-plated (NPTH) holes through the board.

Board.OUTLINE_LINE_SNAP_MM.t: Edge.Cuts line and arc ends closer than this are joined, as KiCad joins them.

Board.OUTLINE_FALLBACK.t: What to do when Edge.Cuts gives no closed outline.
o: Use the hull around all the copper, plus a margin.

Board.OUTLINE_FALLBACK_MARGIN_MM.t: The margin around the copper, when the copper hull stands in for the outline.

Board.OUTLINE_DUPLICATE_AREA_MM2.t: Two closed outlines that differ by less than this area count as one: a ring drawn twice.

Board.OUTLINE_MIN_AREA_MM2.t: A closed outline of this area or less is left out: a line drawn there and back, or a circle of no size.

Copper.COPPER_GROUPING.t: How copper is split into parts, in Simulation mode.
o: One part per net, all its layers and vias joined. What EM ports need.
One part per copper layer, the plating separate.

Copper.COPPER_ENABLED.t: Build the copper, with the plated barrels of holes and vias, and write it to every file.

Copper.DEFAULT_OUTER_FOIL_MM.t: Outer copper thickness when the stack-up gives none.

Copper.DEFAULT_INNER_FOIL_MM.t: Inner copper thickness when the stack-up gives none.

Copper.USE_STACKUP_COPPER_THICKNESS.t: Use each copper layer's thickness from the stack-up where it gives one.

Copper.OUTER_PLATING_ADDED_MM.t: Copper that hole plating adds on the outer layers. Finished outer copper is the foil plus this.
o: Foil only, as KiCad draws it.

Copper.PTH_WALL_MM.t: Plated wall thickness of through-hole pads.

Copper.ETCH_FACTOR.t: Makes traces trapezoids, narrower at the top, as real etching does.
o: Upright walls, as KiCad draws them.
Each wall leans in by half the copper thickness.

Copper.ETCH_STEPS.t: How many stacked slices make up an etched trapezoid.

Copper.ETCH_APPLY_TO_INNER_LAYERS.t: Etch inner copper too, its narrow side toward the board's centre.

Copper.ETCH_UNETCHED_REACH.t: Copper this close to a hole wall or the board edge keeps its drawn outline.
Copper.ETCH_UNETCHED_REACH.n: Measured in etch insets: 1.5 means one and a half.

Copper.HAIRLINE_HOLE_MM.t: Fills the hair-wide gaps KiCad leaves between a zone and a pad of the same net.
Copper.HAIRLINE_HOLE_MM.n: A hole in one net's copper narrower than this on average counts as such a gap.

Copper.CASTELLATION.t: Plated holes that the board edge cuts through.
o: Every plated hole on the edge gets a plated half-barrel, joined to its net.
The same, but only when the board's stack-up says castellated pads.
Not plated: the notch stays bare.
Copper.CASTELLATION.n: KiCad's per-pad Castellated property is not read.

Copper.CASTELLATION_WALL_MM.t: Plated wall thickness of a castellation.

Copper.EDGE_PLATING.t: Copper on the whole routed board edge, for edge connectors and RF shielding.
Copper.EDGE_PLATING.n: The band stops at every hole and castellation on the edge.

Copper.EDGE_PLATING_WALL_MM.t: How thick the edge plating band is, inside the outline.

Copper.EDGE_PLATING_NET.t: Which net the edge copper belongs to.
o: The named net with the most copper touching the edge.
Copper.EDGE_PLATING_NET.n: Copper of other nets inside the band joins it; report.txt lists what moved.

Copper.VIA_TENTING.t: Whether solder mask covers the vias.
o: Follow the board's tenting settings (tented if it has none).
Open the mask over every via.

Copper.HONOUR_REMOVE_UNUSED_LAYERS.t: Follow KiCad's “remove unused layers”: drop via and pad rings on layers nothing connects to.

Copper.COPPER_CONDUCTIVITY_S_PER_M.t: Copper's conductivity, written to materials.json for the solver.

Copper.COPPER_SURFACE_ROUGHNESS_UM.t: Surface roughness, written to materials.json for the solver. It does not change the shapes.

Copper.NO_NET_NAME.t: The net name given to copper on no net: board graphics, unconnected pads.

SolderMask.SOLDER_MASK_ENABLED.t: Build the solder mask and write it to every file.
SolderMask.SOLDER_MASK_ENABLED.n: Off by default: many more solids, and much bigger, slower STEP files.

SolderMask.MASK_OVER_LAMINATE_MM.n: While Use Stackup Mask Thickness is on, the stack-up's value wins.

SolderMask.MASK_OVER_COPPER_MM.t: Mask thickness on top of copper.
SolderMask.MASK_OVER_COPPER_MM.n: While Use Stackup Mask Thickness is on, the stack-up's value wins.

SolderMask.USE_STACKUP_MASK_THICKNESS.t: Use the stack-up's mask thickness, over copper and laminate, on both faces.
SolderMask.USE_STACKUP_MASK_THICKNESS.n: KiCad's stack-up gives one thickness. Off uses Mask Over Laminate and Mask Over Copper.

SolderMask.MASK_EDGE_PULLBACK_MM.t: The mask, and the silkscreen on it, stop this far short of the board edge, as fabs pull them back.

SolderMask.PAD_TO_MASK_CLEARANCE_MM.t: The gap between a pad and its mask opening.
o: Replaces the board setup's value. A pad's or footprint's own margin still wins.

SolderMask.MASK_MIN_WIDTH_MM.t: The narrowest strip of mask kept between two openings. Closer openings are joined, as KiCad plots them.

SolderMask.MASK_WEB_HAIRLINE_MM.t: A strip of mask that the minimum width adds is dropped when it is narrower than twice this.

SolderMask.MASK_OVER_COPPER_HAIRLINE_MM.t: Slivers of mask on copper narrower than twice this are left out. The finish covers them instead.
SolderMask.MASK_OVER_COPPER_HAIRLINE_MM.n: They appear where an opening follows a pad's outline with slightly different points.

SolderMask.MASK_WALL_QUAD_SEGS.t: How round the mask's small walls are where it climbs over a trace, in segments per quarter circle.

Silkscreen.SILKSCREEN_ENABLED.t: Build the silkscreen and write it to every file.
Silkscreen.SILKSCREEN_ENABLED.n: Off by default, like the solder mask.

Silkscreen.SILKSCREEN_OVER_COPPER.t: Ink where the mask is open: on pads, bare copper and openings.
o: Kept as drawn in KiCad, on top of the copper.
Cut off there, as fabs do.

Silkscreen.DRAW_TRUETYPE_TEXT_WITH_STROK.t: Draw text set in a TrueType font with KiCad's stroke font, when the file holds no outline for it.

Silkscreen.INTERLINE_PITCH.t: Line spacing of multi-line text, as a multiple of the text height.
Silkscreen.INTERLINE_PITCH.n: Change these only to match another font.

Silkscreen.INTERLINE_LEGACY_FACTOR.t: KiCad's correction to line spacing for stroke fonts.

Silkscreen.ITALIC_TILT.t: How far italic text leans: the sideways shift per unit of height.

Silkscreen.BOLD_THICKNESS_RATIO.t: Stroke width of bold text, as a share of its width, when the file gives none.

Silkscreen.NORMAL_THICKNESS_RATIO.t: Stroke width of normal text, as a share of its width, when the file gives none.

Silkscreen.MAX_PEN_RATIO.t: A stroke is never wider than this share of the text's smaller size, whatever the file says.

Silkscreen.TEXT_STROKE_QUAD_SEGS.t: How round stroke ends and joins are, in segments per quarter circle.

Silkscreen.DRAW_HIDDEN_TEXT.t: Also draw text the board marks hidden, such as a hidden reference or value.

Silkscreen.SILK_LAYERS.n: Graphics on other layers (Fab, Courtyard, User) are listed as skipped.

Finish.FINISH_ENABLED.t: Build the surface finish on every bare copper face, and write it to every file.
Finish.FINISH_ENABLED.n: Off leaves the bare copper as KiCad draws it.

Finish.FINISH_TYPE.t: Which finish. Its layers are listed under the choice, and you can edit them.
o: One of the eight finishes KESE knows.
Take it from the board's stack-up (Board Setup > Physical Stackup).
Finish.FINISH_TYPE.n: With file, a board that names no finish, or one KESE does not know, stops the run.

Finish.FINISH_GROUPING.t: How the finish is split into parts.
o: One part per side and metal: Top Finish Gold, …
Per side, metal and net: Top Finish Gold_GND, so a solver can pick a net's metals together.

Finish.FINISH_BEFORE_SOLDER_MASK.t: Whether the finish goes on before or after the mask.
o: Before (e.g. full-body hard gold): all outer copper, under the mask and silkscreen.
After, the usual way: only the copper in the openings.

Finish.FINISH_MITRE_LIMIT.t: How far the finish keeps a sharp copper corner's point before cutting it straight across.
o: Corners of 60° or more keep their point; sharper tips are cut.
Every corner is cut at the finish's thickness.

Finish.FINISH_CONDUCTIVITY_S_PER_M.t: Each finish metal's conductivity, written to materials.json.

Geometry.SNAP_GRID_MM.t: Every 2D shape is snapped to this grid, so touching layers share exact corners, with no hairline gaps.

Geometry.SIMPLIFY_TOLERANCE_MM.t: How much copper outlines may be simplified after they are joined.

Geometry.SLIVER_AREA_MM2.t: Polygons smaller than this, left over from cutting and joining shapes, are dropped.

Geometry.ARC_STEP_DEG.t: Arcs are drawn as straight pieces, each turning at most this much.

Geometry.CIRCLE_CHORD_TOLERANCE_MM.t: How far a drawn circle may stray from the true one.

Geometry.CIRCLE_MIN_QUAD_SEGS.t: At least this many straight pieces per quarter circle.

Geometry.CIRCLE_MAX_QUAD_SEGS.t: At most this many straight pieces per quarter circle.

Geometry.TRACK_END_MIN_QUAD_SEGS.t: How round track ends are: at least this many pieces per quarter circle.

Geometry.ELLIPSE_MIN_SEGMENTS.t: An ellipse or elliptical arc has at least this many straight pieces.

Geometry.PINCH_POINT_OPENING_MM.t: Shapes whose edges touch at a single point are opened by this much, so they can be meshed.

Geometry.PINCH_CUT_ROUNDS.t: Tries at opening a pinch point. The cut doubles in size each time.

Geometry.PINCH_DISC_TURN_DEG.t: The shape that cuts a pinch point is turned this far, away from the directions board edges usually run.

Geometry.PINCH_DISC_SIDES.t: Sides of the shape that cuts a pinch point: 8 makes an octagon.

Geometry.HEIGHT_DIGITS.t: Heights closer than 10⁻ⁿ mm count as one height.

Geometry.VERTEX_SHARING_ROUNDS.t: Stage 6 shares corners between a part's slices until nothing changes, at most this many times.
Geometry.VERTEX_SHARING_ROUNDS.n: Most parts settle in one to three rounds. A part still changing is noted in report.txt.

Geometry.NODING_ROUNDS.t: Shapes are snapped to the grid again until they stop changing, at most this many times. One or two in practice.

Geometry.TRIANGULATE_CELL_POINTS.t: A polygon with more points than this is cut into triangles strip by strip, which is much faster when it has many holes.

Geometry.TRIANGULATE_CELL_MM.t: Width of the strips a big polygon is cut into before it is made into triangles. KiCad cuts big polygons into 1 cm cells the same way.

Geometry.SKIN_BURIED_TEST_OFFSET_MM.t: Visual mode: a face is dropped if a point this far outside it lies inside another solid.

Geometry.MESH_MERGE_DIGITS.t: Triangle corners smaller than 10⁻ⁿ rad count as none in smooth shading.

Geometry.FLAT_FACET_THRESHOLD.t: Two faces count as one flat facet when (edge radius ÷ edge span)² is above this.

Geometry.SMOOTH_FACET_AREA_DIVISOR.t: A flat facet bigger than the part's area divided by this keeps flat normals.

Geometry.REACH_MARGIN_STEPS.t: Extra grid steps around the reach of the coating and the ink, where nearby copper is picked out first.
Geometry.REACH_MARGIN_STEPS.n: A bigger margin only picks out more.

Geometry.AIR_NEAR_MARGIN_STEPS.t: The holes' finish: extra grid steps past the finish's reach, where the solid beside the bores is picked out first.
Geometry.AIR_NEAR_MARGIN_STEPS.n: Bores further apart than their reach plus this are not grouped. A bigger margin only picks out more.

Geometry.AIR_TILE_VERTICES.t: The holes' finish: big regions beside the bores are first cut into tiles of about this many corners.
Geometry.AIR_TILE_VERTICES.n: Other values make the same model, except where a corner rounds onto the grid another way.

Geometry.AIR_TILE_DEPTH.t: The holes' finish: at most this many halvings when the regions beside the bores are cut into tiles.

Geometry.FINISH_BORES_AT_A_TIME.t: The holes' finish: bores are worked on in groups of about this many.

Geometry.SKIN_FEW_PIECES.t: Visual skin: up to this many pieces touching a face are cut away one by one; more are cut at once.

Geometry.SKIN_BIG_PIECE_COORDINATES.t: Visual skin: a piece this big or bigger, such as a dielectric with all its via holes, is cut away on its own.

Color.VISUAL_MASK_OPAQUE.t: In Visual mode, draw the mask opaque whatever its alpha. It is a surface there, not a solid.

Color.USE_STACKUP_COLORS.t: Use the mask and silkscreen colours named in the board's stack-up.
o: The board's colours, where it names them.

Color.USER_MASK_OVER_COPPER_LIGHTEN.t: With your own mask colour in the stack-up, Visual mode lightens the mask over copper toward white by this much.

Parallel.WORKERS.t: How many threads or processes work at once.
o: One per processor thread the machine allows.
Everything in turn, in one process.

Parallel.PROCESS_WORKERS.t: At most this many worker processes at once.
Parallel.PROCESS_WORKERS.n: Each needs about 36 MB plus the part it builds: lower it on a machine with little memory.

Parallel.PROCESS_MIN_COORDINATES.t: Worker processes start only for boards at least this big. Smaller boards are faster in one process.
o: Processes for every board of more than one part.

Parallel.GIVE_BACK_MEMORY.t: Hand freed memory back to the system after each step, on Linux. It costs tens of milliseconds.

Parallel.SKIN_PROBES_AT_A_TIME.t: Visual skin: triangles tested at once. Fewer use less memory and take a little longer.

Parallel.VERIFY_TRIANGLES_AT_A_TIME.t: The Verifier: triangles its rays test at once.

Parallel.STEP_ROWS_AT_A_TIME.t: The STEP writer: rows turned into text at once. The file is the same whatever the size.

Parallel.PROCESS_MIN_NETS.t: Copper layers are joined in processes only on boards with this many nets or more. With fewer, threads are as fast.

Parallel.VERIFY_POLYGONS_PER_THREAD.t: Fewer polygons than this are checked in one thread; more are split into groups.

Parallel.VERIFY_GROUPS_PER_WORKER.t: Up to this many groups per worker, so a slow group is made up for by the others.

Parallel.WORKER_STOP_WAIT_S.t: When a run stops its workers (an error, Ctrl+C), how long it waits at most for them to be gone.

Step.STEP_EXACT_ARCS.t: Write circles and arcs as true curves and cylinders.
o: Holes, vias, round pads and arc tracks become true circles and cylinders.
Every curve stays straight pieces, as in the meshes.
Step.STEP_EXACT_ARCS.n: Files come out about 2.5 to 3 times smaller. GLB, STL and OBJ are unchanged.

Step.STEP_ARC_FIT_TOLERANCE_MM.t: Corners within this distance of one circle can form an arc.

Step.STEP_ARC_MIN_POINTS.t: An arc runs through at least this many corners.

Step.STEP_ARC_MIN_SWEEP_DEG.t: An arc turns at least this far in all.

Step.STEP_ARC_MAX_TURN_DEG.t: An arc turns at most this far at one corner, so an octagon or a square stays a polygon.

Step.STEP_ARC_TURN_RATIO_MAX.t: An arc's steps are even: none turns more than this times the median step.

Step.STEP_ARC_TURN_RATIO_MIN.t: No step turns less than this times the median, except the first and last, which a cut may shorten.

Step.STEP_ARC_MAX_SWEEP_DEG.t: Longer arcs are cut into even pieces about this long. A whole circle becomes two arcs.

Step.STEP_ARC_CHECK_FACTOR.t: An arc is dropped where a corner lies further from its circle than this times the fit tolerance.

Step.STEP_STRIP_MAX_TURN_DEG.t: The clear strip checked around an arc has corners at most this far apart.

Step.STEP_TANGENT_MM.t: An edge that cuts into an arc's circle by less than this only touches it, as a tangent does.
Step.STEP_TANGENT_MM.n: OpenCascade treats curves within about 2 × 10⁻⁷ of the unit as touching.

Verifier.VERIFY.t: Check the finished model: closed solids, matching volumes, no overlaps.
f: about 1.5 s more on the examples

Verifier.VERIFY_RAYS.t: Rays cast through a Visual model, along the board's normal, to test its surfaces.

Verifier.VERIFY_VOLUME_TOLERANCE.t: How far a part's volumes, counted different ways, may differ, as a share of the volume, and still pass.

Verifier.VERIFY_VOLUME_NOISE_MM3.t: Extra difference in mm³ allowed on top of Verify Volume Tolerance, whatever the volume.

Verifier.VERIFY_OPENED_VOLUME_MM3.t: How much volume opening pinch points and sharing corners may take from a part, or add, and still pass.

Verifier.VERIFY_MERGE_EXTRA_DIGITS.t: The closed-mesh check merges corners this many digits finer than the snap grid.
